claims.statement: For every 2<=r,s<=20, the polynomial F_r(z) B_s(z)^q with F_r=((1+z)^(r-1)-1)/z and B_s=(1+z)^s+z has finite-order ULC for at least one q in {1,2,3,4}; the least such q occurs 273, 80, 7, and 1 times for q=1,2,3,4, respectively, in the exact census.
claims.scope: Bounded coefficient computation only: 2<=r,s<=20 and q<=4, with the exact coefficients, least finite ULC orders, and blocking indices recorded in ABSORPTION-CENSUS.json and replayed by absorption_census.py. No conclusion beyond this finite grid or about trees.
claims.reason: Exact integer convolution and the necessary-and-sufficient finite-order criterion A_j>0 were applied to all 1444 cases. The replay independently matches the pinned 121 one-factor certificates for 2<=r,s<=12. This establishes only the stated finite computation; a uniform absorption theorem, mixed-factor theorem, convolution application, and graph/selector bridge were not proved.

limitations: Finite scope only: r,s<=20 and at most four absorbed equal-type factors; no arbitrary-arity conclusion.
No proof of a uniform analytic bound on the number of absorbed factors or on the resulting finite ULC orders.
No arbitrary mixed-arity absorption analysis or independent proof of the general finite-ULC convolution theorem and unmarked B_s bounds.
No graph, selector, perturbation, or ordinary-tree aggregate implication was established.
